summary: Walter Ewer worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Fort William College (~1801–1804), served in the Bengal Civil Service (1803–1840), and became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1840.

Walter Friedländer specialized in history/archaeology and Indology, earning a Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber (~1896–1900). He held posts at the German Historical Institute in Rome, Freiburg, Chicago, NYU (1935–1966), and Penn.

Walter Kaufmann studied under Franz Schreker, Curt Sachs, Gustav Becking, and Paul Nettl between 1927 and 1934. In Indology and other fields, he led All India Radio's classical music department (~1937–1946) and taught ethnomusicology at Indiana University (1957–1977).

Active in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Walter Liebenthal earned his doctorate at Breslau (1928–1933) and studied under Otto Strauss, Johannes Nobel, and Max Walleser. He held posts at Peking University, Visva-Bharati, and Tübingen (1964–1982).

Walter M. Spink was a scholar of history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Amherst (~1945–1949) and earned his PhD at Harvard (~1949–1954). He taught at Brandeis (1956–1961) and served as professor at the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

Walter Neisser worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (~1878–1880) and earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1880–1882) under Theodor Benfey and August Fick.
Active in Buddhist studies, Walter Nowick studied at the Juilliard School (~1946–1950) and under Zuigan Goto (1950–1965). He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Petersen worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Yale (~1905–1908). He served at Bethany College (1908), the University of Florida (~1926–1929), and as Associate Professor of Comparative Philology at the University of Chicago (1930).

Walter Porzig, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied under Ernst Windisch, Ferdinand Sommer, and Wilhelm Streitberg. He served as professor at Bern (1925), Jena (1935), Strasbourg (1941–1945), and Mainz (1951).

Walter Ruben studied Indology and philosophy under Heinrich Lüders, Sten Konow, and Hermann Jacobi, taking his doctorate at Bonn (~1921–1924). He was a professor at Ankara (1935–1948), Chile (1948–1950), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke. He held posts at Berlin, the National Library of China, and as Professor of Chinese at London (1947–1960).

Walter Slaje completed his doctorate (~1978–1983) and habilitation (~1983–1993) at the University of Vienna. An Indologist, he served at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and as director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2019).
Walter Sutton Page worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Reader of Bengali at SOAS University of London (~1920–1937) and at the University of Oxford (~1928–1937).

Walter William Skeat was a linguist who was educated at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1854–1858). He subsequently held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1878–1912).

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford (~1902–1907), Oxford (1907–1911), Rennes (~1907–1909), and was a disciple of Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).
Walther Eidlitz was active in Indology and religious studies. He studied building engineering at TU Wien and was a student of his guru, Swami Sadananda (~1946–1957).

Walther Heissig worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Berlin, Vienna (Ph.D. 1936–1941), Göttingen, and Bonn, and taught at Fu Jen, Peking University, and as Central Asian seminar chair at Bonn (1964–1982).

Walther Marcus, a scholar in linguistics and Indology, studied at the University of Giessen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Heidelberg University (~1912–1914), where he earned his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae.

Walther Michaelis worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber (~1893–1898) and served as director at the Francke Foundations (1931–1935).

Walther Prellwitz specialized in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger (~1881–1885), later serving there as Privatdozent (1901) and extraordinary professor of comparative linguistics (1924).
